intro_connection: Connect the adapter to your Home Assistant installation. You will need the IP/hostname and a Long-Lived Access Token from your HASS profile. Sensitive fields are encrypted and shielded from non-admin access.
intro_objects: Choose which object trees the adapter creates and how quickly state changes propagate. The defaults are good for most setups; change them only if you have specific needs.
intro_selection: Home Assistant often exposes hundreds of entities. Pick which ones are relevant to you. Unselected items appear neither in devices.* nor entities.*.
intro_assignment: Map your devices to ioBroker rooms and functions so Alexa, VIS, Material etc. pick them up in the correct room. The adapter never creates new enums — it only uses ones you already have.
intro_mapping: Sometimes an entity is not auto-detected as a known device type, or you want to classify it differently. Override the detection here. The UX mirrors ioBroker.devices.
intro_diagnostics: A health overview of the adapter. Invoke service calls without writing scripts and inspect why an entity is not mapped.
help_host: IP or hostname of your Home Assistant (e.g. homeassistant.local or 192.168.1.10).
help_port: WebSocket API port. Default is 8123; change only if HASS sits behind a reverse proxy.
help_secure: Enable when HASS is served over TLS.
help_access_token: Create one in HASS → Profile → Security → Long-Lived Access Tokens. Valid for 10 years.
help_allow_selfsigned: Only sensible on a trusted LAN. A warning banner will remind you.
help_ca_certificate: Trust an internal CA instead of disabling certificate checks.
help_create_devices_tree: Needed for Alexa, iQontrol, Material adapter and other smart-home surfaces.
help_create_entities_tree: Useful if your scripts directly read HASS attributes. Off by default.
help_auto_include: When HASS discovers a new device, synchronise it automatically. When off, new devices land in the Selection tab for review.
help_debounce_ms: Bursts of updates for the same entity inside this window are collapsed. Higher = fewer writes, slower reaction. Lower = more responsive, more load.
help_write_coalesce_ms: Collapses rapid writes on the same target into a single call_service (e.g. slider drags).
help_response_timeout_ms: Wait this long for HASS to ack a service call before flagging the state as timeout.
help_include_patterns: Glob patterns. If set, only matching entities are synced (e.g. light.*).
help_exclude_patterns: Overrides the device checkbox. Example: sensor.*_signal_strength hides all signal-strength sensors.
hint_assignment_dynamic: The dynamic device/entity assignment view is generated from your live HASS registry. Open the adapter settings while connected to see the table.
hint_mapping_dynamic: The custom mapping view is populated from live HASS entities. Open the adapter settings while connected.
